And for the opponent too, beyond merely pointing out a fault, introducing another [topic] is [a ground for defeat].

'Meaningless' (<s>nirarthaka</s>), like the statement of the sequence of phonemes. For example: 'Sound is eternal because of <s>jabagaḍadaśa</s>-ness, like <s>jhabhañghaḍhadhaṣa</s>.' [The debater] is caught for not employing a means of proof.

This too is incoherent, for the meaninglessness does not arise merely from the statement of the sequence of phonemes, but from the failure to establish the desired object. Whatever constitutes the statement of a non-component of the means of proof -- that alone is meaningless, because of the absence of anything to be expressed that is useful for establishing the provable, and because it is purposeless. Therefore, the adoption of a particular mode [of meaninglessness] is incoherent.

[Objection:] The suffix <s>vat</s> ('like') having been adopted, there is no fault. That is, since the suffix <s>vat</s> has been adopted here in 'like the statement of the sequence of phonemes,' it sometimes also takes something that does not correspond, hence there is no fault. [Reply:] No, because of the absurd consequence of not stating grounds for defeat such as 'another topic.' For then those need not be stated separately, being [already covered] by the statement of what is meaningless.

[Objection:] That which is meaningless is not what is not useful for establishing the provable, but that which has absolutely no meaning whatsoever. [Reply:] Even for a non-debater's statement of what is meaningless, why is there not a ground for defeat, since there is no distinction in the ground for defeat?

[Objection:] No, because there is no occasion for it here. [Reply:] Then it comes to this: whoever states something meaningless here is caught by that very [fault]. And the same applies to everyone who states what is not a component of the means of proof. Every such person, stating what is meaningless, deserves defeat by this very ground for defeat.

And the statement of the sequence of phonemes is not meaningless everywhere, since even that has meaning in some context. Therefore, its meaninglessness here [in the debate context] alone is the ground for defeat.

Moreover, too little is said [by stating that] 'the statement of the sequence of phonemes is a ground for defeat,' since 'clapping the cheek, slapping the side,' and such things should also be stated.

'Unintelligible' (<s>avijñāta-artha</s>): what is not understood even after being stated three times to the assembly and the opponent. A sentence which, even when stated three times to the assembly and the opponent, is not understood -- whether due to ambiguous words, unfamiliar usage, excessively rapid utterance, or such reasons -- that is unintelligible, employed for concealing incapacity, and is a ground for defeat.

This does not differ from the meaningless. If [the speaker] were to make [his statement] relevant to the topic at hand and capable of conveying [meaning], there is no incapacity on his part; [if] the assembly and others do not understand due to stupidity, then the learned person does not deserve defeat.

[Objection:] One who speaks without considering the intelligence of the assembly deserves defeat. [Reply:] When [a speaker] who argues properly speaks out of ignorance, why is the opponent not caught [instead]? If [the debater] is not a winner because of the incapacity to convey [meaning] due to the stupidity of the assembly and others, [he should also] not deserve defeat. When there is an incoherent statement, it is simply meaningless -- hence 'unintelligible' is not a separate ground for defeat.

'Incoherent' (<s>apārthaka</s>): due to the impossibility of syntactic connection, the meaning is unconnected. Where there is no syntactic connection among multiple words or sentences, [and hence] the combined meaning is lost, that is incoherent, like the sentence 'ten pomegranates' [and similar disconnected words].

This, they say, is stated separately from the meaningless [which concerns] unconnected phonemes; but then incoherent sentences should also be stated separately. [Objection:] No, because the incoherent includes both. [Reply:] But then even the meaningless would be included, leading to the same consequence. And the over-extension of enumerating separate definitions of grounds for defeat based on such specific [distinctions] has been stated. And we see no fault in a summary statement, nor any advantage in subdivision -- so all this amounts to nothing.

'Untimely' (<s>aprāptakāla</s>): the statement of the components in a reversed order. When the components such as the thesis and so on have a sequence determined by their definitions and by the nature of the meaning, the statement of the components in reverse order is a ground for defeat.

[Objection:] No, because even so there is establishment. [Reply:] No, because it is like the use of an incorrect word. Just as the word <s>goṇī</s>, used in the meaning of the word <s>gaur</s> ('cow'), conveys the object possessing a hump and so on -- it is not the case that the explanation of the word is useless; through this word one understands the word <s>go</s> itself, and from the word <s>go</s> the object possessing a hump; similarly, through the reversal of the order of the thesis and other components, one understands the [correct] order, and through the order, the meaning. Thus, first the object is adopted, then the instrument, like [taking] a lump of clay and so on in the world.

But this is like a madman's self-description as a madman -- this is like the use of an incorrect word. If from the word <s>goṇī</s> there is understanding of the object possessing a hump, we see no purpose in the effort of word-explanation.

[Objection:] Because of the incapacity of the word <s>goṇī</s> to convey the meaning, the explanation is for the purpose of learning the correct usage. [Reply:] But understanding from the word <s>goṇī</s> is seen in the world. [Objection:] True, it is seen, but not directly. [Reply:] This is said but is not tenable, because for women and <s>Śūdras</s> there is no [double] understanding of both [the incorrect word and then the correct word]. For one who knows both the correct word and the incorrect word understands in this [indirect] way. But one who knows only the word <s>nakka</s> or only the word <s>mukka</s>, and not the word <s>nāsā</s> ('nose') -- how would he, understanding [first] the correct word from the incorrect word, then understand the meaning from [the correct word]? And understanding is seen even for one who does not know both; hence the understanding is not indirect.

And because [a word] that is incapable [of conveying] the meaning is also incapable of generating understanding of [another] word. For the so-called expressiveness (<s>vācakatva</s>) of a word regarding an object is nothing other than the generation of understanding having that object as its content. If an incorrect word can generate understanding of the [correct] word, why can it not generate [understanding] of the object itself? For we see no fear of this [word] from the object that would cause it to avoid [the object].

And because even for one who has not made a convention, [the incorrect word] does not generate understanding of the [correct] word either. For this incorrect word does not generate understanding of the [correct] word by its own nature -- since this is not observed -- but only by convention. And [a word] operating by the force of convention should operate regarding the object itself. For in this way the labor of a chain of understandings is spared.

And because the contrary is observed: in the world, people who do not understand the meaning from the [correct] word are seen extensively learning through incorrect words alone. Hence word-grammar is useless.

[Objection:] It is not useless, because it serves the purpose of learning the correct Sanskrit words. [Reply:] What is this 'correctness' (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of words? For we do not see any 'correctness' of words such as wisdom, strength, learning, and so on; nor is their audibility invariable; nor is there any superiority in conveying meaning. Nor does [correct speech] produce merit, since even from correct [words] used in wrong injunctions demerit arises, and from other [words] in the contrary [situation] merit arises. The proclamation that merely from the correct use of words one enjoys heavenly delights is a mere verbal statement. And such scriptures are not heeded by those who know reasoning. And no one's face turns [in disapproval] at someone who says that merely from incorrect word-use without any injunction of merit-producing [actions] like giving and so on, one falls into hell. Therefore there is no such thing as a 'correct' word.

[Objection:] The usage of the learned (<s>śiṣṭa</s>) is correctness. [Reply:] Who are the learned? Those endowed with qualities such as having known what is to be known, and so on. But what is their unreasonable insistence, independent of any superiority of quality, that they use only these words and not others? And there is no hidden witness regarding words, by which we could determine that the learned do in fact use [only certain words]. Thus we, seeing no superiority of quality, accept the 'correctness' of certain words, or the effort of explaining them, [only] due to the absence of any superiority of quality. And the preservation of the <s>Veda</s> and so on too is purposeless for one who does not abide by that convention. Even if there were a superiority of quality, effort in word-explanation need not be made, since the nature of that [language] is also established from other [sources] -- like the languages of <s>Prākṛt</s>, <s>Apabhraṃśa</s>, <s>Draviḍa</s>, <s>Andhra</s>, and so on. For there is no grammar of the languages in each region, and yet by the force of tradition people understand them in just that way, and [they understand] deviations from their usage just as [they understand deviations from] the usage of Sanskrit words. This preoccupation with the grammar of words is simply the activity of the dull.

Even when the components are in reverse order, if there is understanding of their connection, there is neither reversal nor failure of understanding of the meaning, due to [the inherent] capacity [of the words]. For there is no convention here that 'the components must be employed only in this way' when there is no difference in conveying [meaning].

[Objection:] That very order of theirs is [such that] understanding of the meaning arises from [the components] as they are placed, hence no understanding from reversal; [one must understand] the proper order [first], and then from that the meaning. [Reply:] No, there is no understanding of the proper order from [components] whose connection is not understood. When some connection among words arises -- 'this connects with this here' -- then, with the connection known, what [fixed] order of what with what [is there] by which they would be arranged? When the connection is understood, the order of those [words] is just the connection that is understood among them as they stand. For there is no fixed order of words in sentences -- as 'the servant of the king' or 'of the king, the servant.' When the meaning is completed by however many words, that is one sentence, as '<s>Devadatta</s>, bring the black cow.' Here, even when the words are employed in any order, there is no difference in understanding the meaning -- hence any fixation on order [is groundless].

And it has been demonstrated that even without the thesis-statement, understanding of the meaning as intended will occur. And when a word whose meaning is understood is employed, there is over-extension. And in the remaining [components], having shown the connection, the presence in the property-bearer can be shown, [or] having shown the presence in the property-bearer, the connection can be shown -- there is no fixed rule, since understanding arises in both ways, as stated. And when the connection of words is not understood, even from their [correct] order there is no understanding -- hence this does not differ from the incoherent; and the 'untimely' need not be stated separately.

'Deficient' (<s>hīna</s>): lacking even one component. A statement in which any one of the components such as the thesis and so on is absent -- that statement is deficient, since in the absence of a means of proof, the provable is not established.

[Objection:] Deficiency in the thesis is not [a ground for defeat], since understanding occurs even in its absence -- this has been demonstrated. [Reply:] It is deficient precisely [in the sense that] even in the deficiency there is defeat -- [says] another. [This means:] One who employs a word that is meaningless [since] its meaning is [already] understood deserves defeat. [But] this is an unconsidered statement from one who does not state what is relevant. For this very reason, the thesis is not a component of the means of proof.

'Excessive' (<s>adhika</s>): having more than the reason and example. Since [the function] is accomplished by one, the other is useless -- this should be understood as applying when the restriction [to specific components] is accepted.

Where the inquiry is preceded by the employment of a single proof-statement, there the statement of additional [components] is useless and hence a ground for defeat. But in extended discussion, there is no fault at all, due to the absence of [such] restriction.

'Repetition' (<s>punarukta</s>): the restatement of word or meaning, other than in recapitulation. Verbal repetition: 'sound is impermanent, sound is impermanent.' Meaning-repetition: 'sound is impermanent, sound is subject to cessation.'

Here, verbal repetition need not be stated separately, since it is already covered by the statement of meaning-repetition. For when the meaning differs, there is no fault even if the words are the same, as

yathā vā yad yasmin bhavati bhavati, na bhavati na bhavati,
tat tasya kāryam, itarat kāraṇam iti.
gamyamāna-arthaṃ punarvacanam api punaruktaṃ niyata-
pada-prayoge sādhana-vākye yathā pratijñā-vacanam iti.
artha-punaruktena eva gata-arthatvāt na pṛthag vācyam. ayam
api niyata-sādhana vākya eva doṣo vaktavyaḥ, na vistara-kathāyām,
vyācakṣāṇo hi kadācid asamyak-śravaṇa-pratipatti-
śaṅkayā sākṣi-prabhṛtīnāṃ punaḥ punar brūyāt, api na tatra
kiṃcic chalam.
na aviṣayatvād iti cet, na ayaṃ gurur na śiṣya iti na yatnataḥ
pratipādaniyaḥ, yena punaḥ punar ucyata iti punarvacane
nigraha eva iti cet, na, sākṣiṇāṃ yatnena pratipādyatvāt,
tad-apratipādane doṣa-abhidhānāt, pratipādyasya śiṣyatvāt,
vijigīṣu-vāda-pratiṣedhatvāt, trir-abhidhāna-vacanāt, punarvacana-
prasaṅge samaya-niyama-abhāvāc ca.

na ca idam adhikād bhidyata iti na pṛthag vācyam. viniyata-
pada-prayoge hi sādhana-vākye ādhikya-doṣa iti punarvacane
api gata-arthasya-ādhikyam eva padasya iti.
prapañca-kathāyām apy akathita-eka-artha-sādhana-adhikaraṇāyāṃ
nānā-artha-sādhana-īpsāyāṃ nānā-sādhana-īpsāyāṃ vā
śrotur hetv-ādi-bāhulasya punarvacanasya adoṣatvāt pratīta-
pratyaya-abhāvād hetv-ādi-bāhulyaṃ vacana-bāhulyaṃ ca sādhana-
doṣa iti ādhikya-punarvacanayos tulya-doṣa iti saṃgraha-
vacanaṃ nyāyyam, doṣa-abhāvād eva guṇa-abhāvāt, evaṃprakārānāṃ
bhedānāṃ vacane ca atiprasaṅgād ity uktam.

paryāya-śabda-kalpo hy aparo hetur eka-hetu-pratipādite viṣaye
vartamānaḥ pratipādyasya viśeṣa-abhāvāt. arthaḥ punaḥ-
pratipādanān na bhidyate.
yat punar uktam, anuvāde tv apunaruktaṃ śabda-abhyāsād
artha-viśeṣa-upapatteḥ, yathā hetv-apadeśāt pratijñāyāḥ
punarvacanaṃ nigamanam iti, pratijñāyā eva gamyamāna-arthāyā
vacanaṃ punarvacanam, kiṃ punar asyāḥ punarvacanam
ity ayuktaṃ nigamanam.
vijñātasya parṣadā trir-abhihitasya apratyuccāraṇam ananubhāṣaṇam.
vijñāta-vākya-arthasya parṣadā prativādinā
trir-abhihitasya yad apratyuccāraṇam, tad ananubhāṣaṇaṃ
nāma nigrahasthānam. apratyuccārayan kim-āśrayaṃ para-
pakṣa-pratiṣedhaṃ kuryād iti.

uttareṇa avasānān na idaṃ nigrahasthānam iti cet, syād
etat, uttareṇa guṇa-doṣavatā mūḍha-amūḍhatvaṃ gamyata iti
kiṃ punar-uccāritena. asti hi kaścid uttare samartho na pratyuccāraṇe,
na asau tāvatā nigraham arhed iti.
na, uttara-viṣaya-aparijñānāt. yady ayaṃ na pratyuccārayati,
nirviṣayam uttaraṃ prasajyeta. atha uttaraṃ bravīti,
kathaṃ na uccārayati. tad idaṃ vyāhatam ucyate, na uccārayaty
uttaraṃ ca bravīti iti. apratijñānāc ca. na ca idaṃ pratijñāyate,
pūrvaṃ sarvam uccārayitavyam, paścād uttaram
abhidhātavyam iti, api tu yathākathaṃcid uttaraṃ vācyam,
uttaraṃ ca āśraya-abhāve ayuktam iti, yuktam apratyuccāraṇaṃ
nigrahasthānam iti.

yadi nāma vādī sva-sādhana-artha-vivaraṇa-vyājena prasaṅgād
aparāparaṃ ghoṣayet, vivāda-āspadaṃ ca jijñāsitam
artha-mātram uktvā pratijñā-ādiṣv artha-viśeṣa-paraṃparayā aparān
arthān upakṣipya kathāṃ vistārayet, tac ca sarvaṃ yadā
na anuvaktuṃ śaknuyāt, kas tasya vivāda-āśraya-artha-mātra-uttara-
vacane sāmarthya-vighātaḥ, yena vādi-vacana-ananubhāṣaṇaṃ
nigrahasthānam ucyate. tasmād sarvāṃ vādi-kathām
ananubhāṣamāṇo na uttare asamarthaḥ.
yad-vacana-nāntarīyakā jijñāsita-artha-siddhiḥ yathā pakṣadharmatā-
vyāpti-prasādhana-mātraṃ na tatra api prasaṅga-antara-
upakṣepaḥ, tad avaśyaṃ sādhana-aṅga-viṣayatvād dūṣaṇena upadarśyata
eva. tatra api na sarvaṃ prāg anukrameṇa uccāritavyam,
paścād dūṣaṇaṃ vācyaṃ dvir uccāraṇa-prasaṅgāt. dūṣaṇa-
viṣaya-upadarśana-arthe anubhāṣaṇe vādi-vacana-anukrama-
ghoṣaṇaṃ vyartham iti, na kāryam eva dūṣayatā asya ayaṃ doṣa
iti nāntarīyatvāt pratidoṣa-vacanaṃ viṣaya-upadarśanaṃ
kriyata eva. na hi sarva-viṣaya-upadarśanaṃ kṛtvā yugapad
doṣaḥ śakyate abhidhātum, pratyarthaṃ doṣa-bhedāt. tasmād

yaṃ padārthaṃ dūṣayati, sa eva tad-dūṣaṇa-viṣayas tadā
pradarśanīyo na aparaḥ, tad-dūṣaṇe apara-upadarśanasya asambhavāt.
tasmin dūṣite punar anyo artho apara-doṣa-viṣaya ity
ayam anubhāṣaṇe dūṣaṇe ca nyāyaḥ. sakṛt-sarva-anubhāṣaṇe
api doṣa-vacana-kāle punar viṣayaḥ pradarśanīya eva, apradarśite
doṣasya vaktum aśakyatvāt. tathā ca dvir-anubhāṣaṇaṃ
kṛtaṃ syāt. tatra prathamaṃ sarva-anukrama-anubhāṣaṇaṃ niṣprayojanam.
dūṣaṇa-vādinā dūṣaṇe vaktavye yan na tatra upayujyate,
tasya abhidhānam adoṣa-udbhāvanaṃ dvir-uktiś ca iti
sakṛt-sarva-anubhāṣaṇaṃ parājaya-adhikaraṇaṃ vācyam.

tathā astv iti cet, syād etat, uktaṃ etad artha-antaraṃ nigrahasthānam
iti. tatra sādhane yataḥ kutaścit prasaṅga-ādinā
anāntarīyakā-abhidhānaṃ vādino artha-antara-gamanam eva iti
sa nigrahā-arhaḥ. na kaścit tat-kathita-kriyamāṇa-prasaṅgo
na prasajyate. na api tat tasya anubhāṣaṇīyam, na ca idam apy
asmābhir anujñāyate, sarvaṃ prāk sakṛd vaktavyaṃ paścād
dūṣaṇam iti, kiṃ tu dūṣayatā avaśyaṃ viṣayo darśanīyo
anyathā dūṣaṇā-vṛtter iti.
evaṃ tarhi na ananubhāṣaṇaṃ pṛthag nigrahasthānaṃ
vācyam apratibhayā gatatvāt, uttarasya hy apratipattir
apratibhā. na ca uttara-viṣayam apradarśayann uttaraṃ pratipattuṃ
samarthaḥ. na hy anākṣipta-anuttara-pratipattikam
ananubhāṣaṇam. tena ananubhāṣaṇasya vyāpikāyām apratibhāyāṃ
vihitaṃ nigrahasthānatvam ananubhāṣaṇe labdham
eva, gavi vihitam iva sāsnā-ādimattvaṃ bāhuleye api. tasmād
apratibhā eva nigraha-adhikaraṇatvena vācyā, na ananubhāṣaṇam.

kaś ca ayaṃ samaya-niyamas trir-abhihitasya ananubhāṣaṇam
iti. yadi tāvat para-pratipādana-arthā pravṛttiḥ, kiṃ
trir abhidhīyeta. tathā tathā sa grāhaṇīyaḥ, yathā asya pratipattir
bhavati. atha para-upatāpana-arthā, tadā api kiṃ trir
abhidhīyate, sākṣiṇāṃ karṇe nivedya prativādī kaṣṭa-pratīta-
druta-saṃkṣipta-ādibhir upadrotavyaḥ, yathā-uttara-pratipatti-
vimūḍhas tūṣṇīṃbhavati. na hi para-upatāpana-krame kaścin
nyāyaḥ, yena kaṣṭa-pratīta-prayoga-druta-uccāritāni nivāryante
trir-abhidhānaṃ vā vidhīyate. na ca para-upatāpāya santaḥ pravartante
śāstrāṇi vā praṇīyante ity ado vaktavyam. tasmāt
tāvad vaktavyam, yāvad anena na gṛhītam, na trir eva. agrahaṇa-
sāmarthye prāg eva paricchinna-sāmarthyena parihartavyaḥ
parān anupratibodhyeti.

avijñātaṃ ca ajñānam. vijñātaṃ parṣadā prativādinā yad
avijñātam, tad ajñānaṃ nāma nigrahasthānam. arthe khalv
avijñāte na tasya pratiṣedhaṃ brūyād iti.
etad apy ananubhāṣaṇa-vad apratibhayā eva gamyatvād
avācyam. yathā ananubhāṣaṇe apradarśita-viṣayatvād uttara-
pratipattir aśakyā iti anuttara-pratipattyā eva nigrahasthānatvam
uttara-viṣaya-pradarśana-prasaṅgam antareṇa anubhāṣaṇasya
vaiyarthyāt, tathā-jñāne apy uttara-apratipattyā eva
nigrahasthānatvam, ajānānaḥ katham uttaram uttara-viṣayaṃ
ca uttaraṃ brūyād iti viṣaya-ajñānam uttara-jñānaṃ
ca nigrahasthānam, anyathā-pratibhāyā nirviṣayatvāt. anavadhārita-
artho hi na anubhāṣet. ananubhāṣamāṇo viṣayam
apradarśya-uttaraṃ pratipattuṃ na śaknuyād iti uttaraṃ
na pratipadyeta jñāta-uttara-tad-viṣayasya uttara-apratipatter asambhavāt.

ubhayam etad uttara-apratipatteḥ kāraṇam iti.
tad-abhāve pratipattir bhavaty eva iti tayoḥ pṛthag vacane
apratibhāyāḥ ko viṣaya iti vaktavyam, nirviṣayatvād avācyā
eva syāt.
na uttara-ajñānam ajñānaṃ kiṃ tarhi viṣaya-ajñānam, ajñāte
hi viṣaye uttara-ajñānāt tan na pratipadyeta iti asti viṣayo apratibhāyā
iti cet, evaṃ tarhy ananubhāṣaṇaṃ nirviṣayam,
ajñānena ākṣepāt. na hi viṣayaṃ samyak pratipadyamānaḥ
kaścin na anubhāṣeta iti na ananubhāṣaṇaṃ pṛthag vācyam.
uttara-ajñānasya ca ākṣepāt. viṣaya-ajñānena uttara-ajñānam apy
ākṣiptam eva. na hi viṣayam ajānann uttaraṃ jānāti iti na eva apratibhāyā
viṣayo asti.

jñāte api viṣaye punar uttara-ajñānam apratibhāyā viṣaya
iti cet, evaṃ tarhi viṣaya-uttara-ajñānayor api prabhedān nigrahasthāna-
antarāṇi vācyāni. yathā ajñānasya viṣaya-ajñānam uttara-
ajñānam iti prabhedād asaty api guṇa-atiśaye nigrahasthāna-
antara-vyavasthā kriyate, tathā ajñānayor api sarvā-jñāna-ardha-
ajñānam ity ādi-prabhedān nigrahasthāna-antarāṇi kiṃ na ucyante.
na ca ubhayasya apy ajñānasya saṃgraha-vacane kaścid
doṣaḥ, guṇas tu syād iti saṃgraha-vacanaṃ nyāyyam.
tasmād ananubhāṣaṇa-jñānayor apratibhā-viṣayatvān na
pṛthag-vacanam. api ca na pūrva-uttara-vādino hetv-ābhāsā-pratibhābhyām
anyan nigrahasthānaṃ nyāyyam asti tad-ubhaya-
vacanena eva sarvam uktam iti. tad-ubhaya-ākṣipteṣu prabhedeṣu
guṇa-atiśayam antareṇa vacana-āder atiprasaṅgād vyarthaḥ
prapañca iti.

uttarasya apratipattir apratibhā. para-pakṣa-pratiṣedha
uttaraṃ yadā na pratipadyate, tadā nigṛhīto vaktavyaḥ.
sādhana-vacana-anantaraṃ prativiṣayam uttare vyarthaṃ
tad-ajñāna-krama-ghoṣaṇa-śloka-pāṭha-ādinā kālaṃ gamayan kartavya-
apratipattyā nigraha-arha iti nyāyyaṃ nigrahasthānam
iti.
kārya-vyāsaṅgāt kathā-vicchedo vikṣepaḥ. yat kiṃcit kartavyaṃ
vyāsajya kathāṃ vicchinatti, idaṃ me karaṇīyaṃ
parihīyate, asminn avasite paścāt kariṣyāmi, pratiśyāyakalā
me kaṇṭhaṃ kṣiṇoty evam-ādinā kathāṃ vicchinatti, sa vikṣepo
nāma nigrahasthānam. ekatara-nigraha-antāyāṃ kathāyāṃ
svayam eva kathā-antaṃ pratipadyata iti.

idam apy yadi pūrvapakṣa-vādī kuryād vyāja-upakṣepa-mātreṇa,
na punar bhūtasya tathāvidha-kathā-uparodhinaḥ kāryasya
bhāve, tasya sva-sādhana-asāmarthya-paricchedād eva
vikṣepaḥ syāt. tathā ca idam artha-antara-gamana eva antarbhaved
asamartha-sādhana-abhidhānād hetv-ābhāseṣu vā. prakṛta-
sādhana-asambaddha-pratipatteś ca nirarthaka-apārthakābhyāṃ
na bhidyate. atiprasaṅgaś ca evaṃprakārāṇām asambaddha-
sādhana-vākya-pratipatti-bhedānāṃ pṛthag-nigrahasthāna-
vyavasthāpane proktaḥ. atha uttarapakṣa-vādy evaṃ vikṣipet,
tasya api sādhana-anantaram uttare pratipattavye tad-apratipattyā
vikṣepa-pratipattir apratibhāyām artha-antare vā antarbhavati.

nanu na avaśyaṃ sādhana-dūṣaṇābhyām eva sarvasya pratipattir,
yena sarvā vādi-prativādinor na asamyak-pratipattir
hetv-ābhāseṣv apratibhāyāṃ vā antarbhavet. bhavati hi anibaddhena
api kathā-prapañcena vivāda iti, na, asambhavāt.
ekatra adhikaraṇe viruddha-abhyupagamayor vivādaḥ syāt, aviruddha-
abhyupagamayor anabhyupagamayor vā vivādā-abhāvāt.
tatra avaśyam ekasya prāg-vacana-pravṛttiḥ, yugapat-pravṛttau
paraspara-vacana-śravaṇa-avadhāraṇa-uttarāṇām asambhavena
pravṛtti-vaiphalyāt svastha-ātmanām apravṛtteḥ. tena
ca sva-upagama-upanyāse avaśyaṃ sādhanaṃ vaktavyam,
anyathā pareṣām apratipatteḥ, apareṇa ca tat-sambandhi dūṣaṇam.

ubhayor asamyak-pratipattau hetv-ābhāsa-apratibhayoḥ
prasaṅga iti. sarvo nyāya-pravṛttaḥ pūrva-uttarapakṣa-upanyāso
dvayaṃ na atipatati. etena eva vitaṇḍā pratyukta-abhyupagama-
abhāve vivāda-abhāvāt.
yadā tarhy abhyupagamya vādaṃ viphalatayā na kiṃcid
vakti, anyad vā yat kiṃcit pralapati, tadā kathaṃ hetv-ābhāsa-
antarbhāvaḥ. asamarthita-sādhana-abhidhāna evam uktam,
anabhidhāna anya-abhidhānayor api parājaya eva ity uktam
abhyupagamya vādam asādhana-aṅga-vacanāt. etena adhikasya
punaruktasya ca pratijñā-āder vacanasya ca nigrahasthānatvaṃ
vyākhyātam, tad api hi pratipādita-artha-viparyayatvāt
sādhana-sāmarthya-anabhidhānam. apratīta-pratyayatayā lakṣaṇāt
sādhanasya asādhana-aṅga-vacanam iti nigrahasthānam
iti.

sva-pakṣa-doṣa-abhyupagamāt para-pakṣe doṣa-prasaṅgo mata-anujñā.
yaḥ pareṇa coditaṃ doṣam anuddhṛtya, bhavato
apy ayaṃ doṣa iti bravīti, yathā bhavāṃś cauraḥ puruṣatvād
ity ukte sa taṃ pratibrūyād, bhavān api iti, sa sva-pakṣe doṣa-abhyupagamāt
para-pakṣe taṃ doṣaṃ prasañjayan para-matam
anujānāti iti mata-anujñā nigrahasthānam iti.
atra api yadi puruṣatvāc cauro bhavān api syāt, na ca bhavatā
ātmā evam iṣṭaḥ, tasmān na ayaṃ caurya-hetur iti yady
ayam abhiprāyaḥ, tadā na kaścid doṣaḥ, anabhimate tad-ātmani
cauratvena hetu-darśanena dūṣaṇāt.

prasaṅgam antareṇa āñjasena eva kiṃ na vyabhicārita iti
cet, yat kiṃcid etat, santi hy evaṃprakārā api vyavahārā loka
iti. atha tad upakṣepam abhyupagacchaty eva, tadā apy
asāv uttara-apratipattyā eva tat-sādhane nigraha-arhaḥ, na aparatra
sva-doṣa-upakṣepāt, tat-sādhana-nirdoṣatāyāṃ hi tad-abhyupagama
eva uttara-apratipattir iti tāvatā eva pūrvam āpanna-nigrahasya
para-doṣa-upakṣepasya anapekṣaṇīyatvād iti.
nigraha-prāptasya anigrahaḥ paryanuyojya-upekṣaṇam. paryanuyojyo
nāma nigraha-upapattyā codanīyaḥ, tasya upekṣaṇaṃ
nigraha-prāpto asi ity ananuyogaḥ. etac ca kasya parājaya
ity anuyuktayā parṣadā vaktavyam, na khalu nigraha-prāptaḥ
sva-kaupīnaṃ vivṛṇuyād iti.

atra api yadi sādhana-vādinaṃ nigraha-prāptam uttara-vādī
na paryanuyuṅkte, apratibhā eva asya uttara-apratipatter iti na
paryanuyojya-upekṣaṇaṃ pṛthag nigrahasthānam. nyāya-cintāyāṃ
punar na dvayor ekasya api atra jaya-parājayau, sādhana-
ābhāsena artha-apratipādanād bhūta-doṣa-anabhidhānāc ca.
atha kaṃcid doṣam udbhāvayati, kaṃcin na, na tadā
nigraham arhati uttara-pratipatteḥ.
arhati eva, sarvasya sato doṣasya anudbhāvanād iti cet, na
santa iti kṛtvā sarve doṣā avaśyaṃ vaktavyā avacane vā
nigrahaḥ, ekena api tat-sādhana-vighātād, eka-sādhana-vacana-vat.

yathā ekasya artha-asya aneka-sādhana-sadbhāve apy ekena eva
tat-siddher na sarva-upādānam iti na doṣam udbhāvayann eva aparasya
anudbhāvanān nigraha-arhaḥ.
atha pūrva-pakṣa-vādī uttara-pakṣa-vādinaṃ nigraha-prāptaṃ
na nigṛhṇāti, tadā tayor nyāyena na ekasya api pūrvavaj
jaya-parājayau. doṣa-ābhāsaṃ brūvānam uttara-vādinaṃ sva-
sādhanād anutsārayato asamarthita-sādhana-aṅgatvān na jayo
vādinaḥ, sarva-doṣa-asambhava-pradarśanena sādhana-aṅga-samarthanāt.
na apy uttara-vādino bhūta-doṣa-apratipādanāt. tasmād
evam api na paryanuyojya-upekṣaṇaṃ nāma parājaya-adhikaraṇam
iti.

asthāne nigrahasthāna-anuyogo niranuyojya-anuyogaḥ. nigrahasthāna-
lakṣaṇasya mithyā-avasāyād anigrahasthāne nigṛhīto
asi iti bruvan niranuyojya-anuyogān nigṛhīto vaktavyaḥ.
atra api yadi tat-sādhana-vādinam abhūtair doṣair uttara-
vādy abhiyuñjīta, so asthāne nirdoṣe nigrahasthānasya abhiyokta-
udbhāvayitā na bhavati. tathā ca bhūta-doṣa-udbhāvana-lakṣaṇasya
uttarasya apratipatter itareṇa uttara-ābhāsatve pratipādite
apratibhayā eva nigṛhīta iti na idam ato nigrahasthāna-antaram.
atha uttara-vādinaṃ bhūtaṃ sādhana-doṣam udbhāvayantam
aparo doṣa-ābhāsa-vacanena abhiyuñjīta, tasya tena bhūta-
doṣatve pratipādite sādhana-ābhāsa-vacanena eva nigṛhīta iti.

evam api na idaṃ hetv-ābhāsebhyo bhidyate. avaśyaṃ hi
viṣaya-antara-vyāpty-arthaṃ hetv-ābhāsā nigrahasthānatvena
vaktavyāḥ, tad-uktāv apara-uktir anarthakā iti.
siddhāntam abhyupetyā-niyamāt kathā-prasaṅgo apasiddhāntaḥ.
kasyacid arthasya tathābhāvaṃ pratijñāya pratijñātā-
artha-viparyayāt kathā-prasaṅgaṃ kurvato apasiddhānto
vijñeyaḥ. yathā na sato vināśaḥ, na asad utpadyata iti siddhāntam
abhyupetya pakṣam avasthāpayati ekā prakṛtir
vyaktasya, vikārāṇām anvaya-darśanāt. mṛd-anvayānāṃ śarāva-
ādīnāṃ dṛṣṭam eka-prakṛtikatvam, tathā ca ayaṃ vyakta-
bhedas sukha-duḥkha-moha-samanvito gṛhyate. tat sukha-ādibhir
eka-prakṛtir iti. sa evam uktavān paryanuyujyate.

atha prakṛtir vikāra iti kathaṃ lakṣayitavyam iti. yasya avasthitasya
dharma-antara-nivṛttau dharma-antaraṃ pravartate,
sā prakṛtiḥ. yat tad dharma-antaram, sa vikāra iti. so ayaṃ
prakṛta-artha-viparyayād aniyamāt kathāṃ prasañjayati. pratijñātaṃ
khalv anena na asad āvirbhavati, na sat tirobhavati iti.
sad-asatoś ca tirobhāva-āvirbhāvāv antareṇa na kasyacit pravṛtty-
uparamaḥ pravṛttir vā iti evaṃ pratyavasthito yadi sata
ātma-hānam asataś ca ātma-lābham abhyupaiti, apasiddhānto
bhavati atha na abhyupaiti, pakṣo asya na sidhyati iti.

iha api na kaścid aniyamāt kathā-prasaṅgaḥ yat tena upagatan
na asad utpadyate, na sad vinaśyati iti tasya samarthanāya
idam uktam eka-prakṛtikam idaṃ vyaktam anvaya-darśanād
iti. tatra ekā prakṛtiḥ sukha-duḥkha-mohaḥ. tad-avibhakta-
yonikam idaṃ vyaktaṃ tad-anvaya-darśanāt. vyaktasya
tat-svabhāvatā-bheda-upalabdher iti sukha-ādīnām utpatti-
vināśa-abhyupagama-abhāvāt sarvasya tad-ātmakasya na utpatti-
vināśāv iti siddhaṃ bhavati. atra tad-uktasya hetor doṣam
anudbhāvya vikāra-prakṛti-lakṣaṇaṃ pṛcchan svayam ayaṃ
prakṛta-asambandhena aniyamāt kathāṃ pravartayati.

tatra idaṃ syād vācyam, vyaktaṃ nāma pravṛtti-nivṛtti-
dharmakam, na tathā sukha-ādayaḥ. vyaktasya sukha-ādy-anvaye
sukha-ādi-svabhāvatāyāṃ pravṛtti-nivṛtti-dharmatā-lakṣaṇam
avahīyata iti. na tad-rahita-sukha-ādi-svabhāvatā vyakta-lakṣaṇa-
virodhād iti. sukha-ādy-anvaya-darśanād ity asiddho hetur
iti. evaṃ hi tasya sādhana-doṣa-udbhāvanena pakṣo dūṣito
bhavati. so anupasaṃhṛtya sādhana-doṣaṃ kathāṃ pratānayan
sva-doṣaṃ paratra upakṣipati.
ayam eva doṣo anena prakaraṇena ucyata iti cet, eṣa naimittikāṇāṃ
viṣayaḥ, na lokaḥ śabdair apratipāditam arthaṃ
pratipattuṃ samartha iti. sa eva ayaṃ bhaṇḍālekhyanyāyo
atra api. yathoktena nyāyena pūrvakasya asādhana-aṅgasya asiddhasya
hetor abhidhānād eva nigrahaḥ, na api aniyamāt
kathā-prasaṅgād iti. idam api hetv-ābhāseṣv antarbhāvān na
pṛthag vācyam.

hetv-ābhāsāś ca yathoktāḥ. hetv-ābhāsāś ca nigrahasthānāni.
kiṃ punar lakṣaṇa-antara-yogād hetv-ābhāsā nigrahasthāna-
bhāvam āpadyante, yathā pramāṇāni prameyatvam
ity ata āha yathokta-hetv-ābhāsa-lakṣaṇena eva nigrahasthāna-
bhāva iti.
atra api yathoktaṃ kṛtvā cintyam eva, kiṃ te yathālakṣita-prabhedās
tathā eva, āhosvid anyathā iti. tat tu cintyamānam
iha atiprasajyata iti na pratanyate. hetv-ābhāsāś ca yathānyāyaṃ
nigrahasthānam iti etāvan-mātram iṣṭam iti.
